reason: A tester install guide was only trustworthy after its steps were run literally as a new user in an isolated home. No existing skill covers that technique; it is a general class (checking install or setup docs), so it is born as an umbrella for future install-doc checks.
The start demo verified the written MCP entry two ways that cost no model call; the method belongs in the scratch-install checklist so the next install check repeats it.

The episode verified a shipped command's side effects by wheel install, network-blocked strace and a before/after home snapshot; this is the install-verification class, so the technique belongs in the existing scratch-home skill.

This episode's install walkthrough re-derived four things the skill did not say: the before/after comparison method via a HEAD worktree, the scratch home must exist before METAFORM_HOME points at it (the second run failed on exactly that), the shipped README must be read from the built zip, and a failing stand-in agent is the way to test the failed-start path.
Absorbed into verify-change-proof as its install-steps subsection.
